confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer anchors on crowd-sourced cost-of-living data for Ohrid from mylifeelsewhere.com. Those figures vary between pages, with beer at about $2.1–2.9, a cappuccino at about $2.0–2.2 and an inexpensive meal at about $6–8. I also nudged them up for peak summer tourist season in July. The mid-range meal for two is an estimate based on the inexpensive-meal level and wider Balkan price patterns. I did not search directly for cocktail and wine prices, so I estimated them from their usual local price relationship to beer. My accommodation figures are general-knowledge estimates for a lakeside resort town in July peak season. I did not check any booking sites or current listings, so these figures are the least certain. The FX observation of 0.6720 for 2026-11-18 comes from a web search summary that says the RBA page shows this figure. A secondary aggregator gave the same number, but I did not open the RBA page itself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Ohrid is a seasonal lake resort and costs a bit more than the North Macedonian average for restaurants. I compared it with Balkan tourist towns such as Budva-lite or Berat and adjusted upward from Skopje price levels.
